works.name: The End of the F***ing World

podcast.title: Controversial Role in Think Tank (2003) Recording
podcast.body: Despite not being a full public member of Blur during the recording of Think Tank, Graham Coxon significantly complicated the recording process due to his personal issues and disruptive behavior. "el papel que juega graza en cocción dentro de este disco, porque aunque no estaba dentro del grupo de los públicos finalmente, dio bastante por saco."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Deleted Guitar Recordings from Think Tank (2003)
podcast.body: Graham Coxon recorded guitar parts for several songs on Think Tank, but these were ultimately deleted from the final album, leaving him with only one credited contribution. "él hizo algunas grabaciones de guitarras y otras canciones que finalmente fueron eliminadas."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Absence from Initial Reunion Meeting
podcast.body: Graham Coxon's absence from Blur's initial reunion meeting in London significantly contributed to the overall tension surrounding the band's decision to record a new album. "graza en cocción ni siquiera se presentó."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Antidepressant Treatment and Alcoholism During Recording
podcast.body: During his brief time in the studio for Think Tank, Graham Coxon was simultaneously on antidepressant treatment and constantly drunk, leading to numerous problems and eccentric behavior that made it practically impossible for the band to work with him. "Él estaba en pleno tratamiento de el antidepresivo y sobre todo él estaba borracho todo el día, entonces tenía un montón de problemas y sobre todo un comportamiento bastante exténtrico, lo cual hizo que prateía el impossible trabajar con él."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Band's Acceptance of Coxon's Return
podcast.body: Despite his earlier absence, the band accepted Graham Coxon's return to the studio, acknowledging his importance as a key member, referred to as the "second pilálogo" (second pillar). "graza en cocción es el segundo pilálogo y ellos lo afectaron bastante bien."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Coxon's Disinterest in Tarle
podcast.body: Graham Coxon was completely disinterested in 'Tarle', which contributed to his discontent with the album's direction and his minimal creative input. The exact nature of 'Tarle' (song, concept, etc.) is not specified. "Graza en cocción estaba en la gran disto por Tarle y eso no había nada que hacer."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Disastrous Return to Recording
podcast.body: Graham Coxon's return to the Think Tank recording sessions quickly devolved into a disaster due to his ongoing personal struggles and behavior. "El problema es que eso fue un auténtico desastre."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Introduction to Jamie Hewlett
podcast.body: Graham Coxon of Blur was a big fan of Jamie Hewlett's work. He introduced Damon Albarn to Jamie, leading to their eventual collaboration on Gorillaz. "Graham became a big fan of Jamie's work. And after Graham introduced Damon to Jamie, they became acquaintances."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Manager Demands Coxon's Departure
podcast.body: Due to his disruptive and impossible behavior, the band's manager ultimately instructed Graham Coxon to leave the group during the Think Tank sessions and allow them to work in peace, a decision the rest of the band agreed to as the situation had become untenable. "el manayer acabó diciendo a la grabación cocción que se fuese de el grupo y se marcha si lo dejase trabajar tranquilos, a lo que el resto del grupo accedió porque la situación era rádia en imposibilidad."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Personal Struggles and Discontent with Album Direction
podcast.body: Graham Coxon was not only in a very bad personal state but was also highly discontent with the direction the Think Tank album was taking, particularly with Damon Albarn's dominance and the album's electronic shift. "Graza en cocción no solo estará en un punto muy malo de subir a personal, sino que encima estaba muy descontento como unas cosas que estaban pasando por el disco."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Prolific Solo Career
podcast.body: During Blur's hiatus, Graham Coxon pursued a quite prolific solo career. "graza en cocción tuvo una carrera bastante proliscina en Solitario."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Rehabilitation for Alcoholism and Depression
podcast.body: During the initial recording phases of Think Tank, Graham Coxon was undergoing rehabilitation for severe alcoholism and depression, a fact unknown to the band at the time. "graza en cocción estaba rehabilitándose dentro de una alcoholismo y depresión por los que estaba muy mal, pero el grupo no lo sabía y en un caso lo llegó a decir."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Unexpected Return to Studio
podcast.body: After Blur had begun recording Think Tank without him, Graham Coxon unexpectedly appeared at the studio one day and decided to start recording with the band. "un día graza en cocción se presenta allí como quien no tiene la cosa y el tío decide empezar a grabar con ellos."

srcs.episode: Blur - Think Tank y su dificil grabación.

podcast.title: Unused Vocals for Humans Album
podcast.body: Graham Coxon recorded vocals for the Gorillaz album "Humans," but his parts were ultimately not used on the final record. "Same thing happened with some vocals from Blur Band-made Grain Coxon."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Connection to Gorillaz Creators
xref.body: Jarvis Cocker of Pulp knew Jamie Hewlett. He also introduced Graham Coxon of Blur to Jamie Hewlett, which eventually led to Damon Albarn and Jamie Hewlett becoming acquaintances and later collaborating on Gorillaz. "So Jamie knew Jarvis Cocker of Pulp, obviously. And Jarvis was a maid of Graham Cox and a blur."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
